findings.title: Materials' 100% growth bet is extreme
findings.body: Materials trades at 15.24x forward versus 30.46x trailing, a 50 percent compression that implies 100 percent earnings growth. That is the widest lens gap in the table, and it puts the forward multiple at the 12th percentile of its five-year range while the trailing sits near the middle. The market is pricing a doubling of earnings that the trailing record does not support.

findings.title: Health Care's 80% growth assumption is aggressive
findings.body: Health Care's forward multiple is 19.08x, 45 percent below its trailing 34.43x, implying 80 percent earnings growth. The forward percentile has dropped 19 points in both the past week and month, yet the multiple still sits at the 81st percentile. Analysts are underwriting a sharp margin expansion that has no visible basis in reported earnings.

findings.title: Utilities' forward premium is a warning
findings.body: Utilities' trailing P/E sits at the 0th percentile of its five-year range, the cheapest it has been, while the forward multiple is at the 19th percentile. The 19-point gap between lenses is entirely a bet on 4 percent earnings growth, which is hardly a catalyst. The sector looks cheap on reported earnings, but the forward lens says the market is not rewarding it.
